title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
claim: LnCC-catalyzed cycloaddition of CO2 to epoxides follows Lewis-acid activation of the epoxide oxygen, nucleophilic ring opening, CO2 capture by the opened alkoxide, and ring closure to the cyclic carbonate.
explanation: The review presents this sequence as the general mechanism and then uses Ln–Zn cluster examples to show that two nearby Lewis-acidic metals can share epoxide activation and nucleophilic assistance. Lanthanide performance is linked to oxophilicity and high Lewis acidity, with ionic radius as an additional steric handle.
scope: Lanthanide and 3d–4f cluster catalysts, usually with a bromide nucleophile such as TBAB, for cyclic-carbonate synthesis.
conditions: Typically TBAB cocatalyst; pressures from 0.1 to 1 MPa and temperatures from 25 to 120 °C depending on the cluster.
caveats: A nucleophilic cocatalyst is part of the stated mechanism; activity without TBAB is not established by this summary.
